lines.cap: Nothing ever stuck to him. Until his right-hand man started singing.

lines.cap: John Gotti. Boss of the Gambino family, New York's most powerful mafia clan, from 1985.
lines.say: John Gotti. Boss of the Gambino family, New York's most powerful mafia clan, from 1985.

lines.cap: He took over by having his own boss shot dead outside a steakhouse in Manhattan. Days before Christmas.
lines.say: He took over by having his own boss shot dead outside a steakhouse in Manhattan. Days before Christmas.

lines.cap: Then he became a celebrity. Thousand dollar suits. Perfect hair. Smiling for the cameras. The press called him the Dapper Don.
lines.say: Then he became a celebrity. Thousand dollar suits. Perfect hair. Smiling for the cameras. The press called him the Dapper Don.

lines.cap: Prosecutors took him to court three times. Three times he walked free. Now they called him the Teflon Don. Nothing stuck.
lines.say: Prosecutors took him to court three times. Three times he walked free. Now they called him the Teflon Don. Nothing stuck.

lines.cap: But the FBI bugged an apartment above his social club. And caught him talking. A lot.
lines.say: But the FBI bugged an apartment above his social club. And caught him talking. A lot.

lines.cap: Then his underboss, Sammy the Bull Gravano, flipped. He testified against Gotti, and admitted to nineteen murders himself.
lines.say: Then his underboss, Sammy the Bull Gravano, flipped. He testified against Gotti, and admitted to nineteen murders himself.

lines.cap: In 1992, Gotti got life in prison, with no parole. He died there ten years later.
